STILLROOT'S SONG   |   GM DOSSIER

Hekate-inspired material

This optional scene uses a fantasy adaptation, not a claim that the historical goddess is an evil hag or that one modern interpretation exhausts her ancient roles.

In Hesiod's Theogony (approximately lines 411-452), Hekate receives honour and influence across earth, sea and heaven. In the Homeric Hymn to Demeter, she assists Demeter with torches and later accompanies Persephone. These primary texts support using a torch-bearing guide at a boundary. Do not present the earlier 'past, present, future' explanation of her triple form as an established universal ancient meaning.

Optional dream shrine

Three narrow paths meet around a weathered post. A key hangs from it. Two lamps burn with steady flames, though everything around them moves with the dream.

Beneath the key someone has written: A DOOR MAY OPEN BOTH WAYS.

There is no test of a player's real religion. The shrine offers a meaningful choice: continue, return to the refuge, or help a lost memory find its name. Lighting a lamp for a specific forgotten person grants one Lucid token, once. It is not necessary to harm an animal or enact a real-world ritual.

Historical references

Hesiod, Theogony, H. G. Evelyn-White translation: https://www.theoi.com/Text/HesiodTheogony.html

Homeric Hymn to Demeter passages, collected with source citations: https://www.theoi.com/Khthonios/Hekate.html

All encounter mechanics and inscriptions here are invented for Stillroot.
